offence_severity: Death sentence to imprisonment for 20 years
physical_harm: Five persons died, including three children, due to multiple injuries
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning based on the motive and the conduct of the accused
motive: Quarrel with deceased 'S' on the day of Eid
key_evidence_accepted: The deaths established as homicidal in nature, evidence of witnesses, extra-judicial confession, absconding of accused, his conduct at the time of his arrest, recoveries of incriminating articles made pursuant to disclosure statement, the motive and the statement of accused u/s 313 CrPC, all connect him to the crime and establish his guilt
witness_credibility: The entire evidence of PWs 1 and 4, though they did not witness the occurrence, as rightly observed by the High Court, the manner in which they deposed before the court and the details stated by them are acceptable and there is no valid reason to disbelieve their statements. Their evidence very clearly establishes that the appellant-accused was the person who was involved in the incident occurred
post_offence_conduct: absconding from the scene would establish his guilt and rule out hypothesis of innocence. It has come out from the evidence that immediately after the incident, the accused left the village and boarded a bus to Delhi. However, he was arrested in the way by PW-16 at 2.20 a.m., on 28.10.2006. There is no proper explanation by the appellant-accused even u/s 313 statement for his sudden departure from the scene and going to Delhi. In the absence of any reason, the conduct of the appellant supports the case of the prosecution. Further, the appellant, when questioned by PW-16 in the bus, suppressed his original name and gave a false name and only on further interrogation, disclosed his original name. These aspects go against his conduct and support the case of the prosecution
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 27-10-2006; Trial judgment: 13.12.2007; High Court decision: 05.03.2008; Supreme Court decision: APRIL 18, 2013
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Pijush K. Roy, Kakali Roy; Counsel for the State: Archana Pathak Dave, Dr. Sumant Bharadwaj, Ankita Chaudhary, Mridula Ray, Milind Kumar
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted and sentenced to death; High Court: Upheld conviction, commuted death sentence to life imprisonment with 20 years' restriction; Supreme Court: Affirmed High Court's decision
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant was responsible for the gruesome murders of five persons, including three children, based on circumstantial evidence, extra-judicial confession, recovery of incriminating articles, motive, and the accused's conduct at the time of arrest.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no direct eye witness to the incident, the prosecution's case rested on circumstantial evidence, and there were contradictions in the FIR and witness statements. They also contended that the High Court was not justified in restricting remission before 20 years of imprisonment.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that life imprisonment, when imposed for heinous crimes, should be subject to restrictions on remission to ensure the punishment is proportionate and serves the purpose of justice.
precedent_relied_upon: Shri Bhagwan vs. State of Rajasthan, Prakash Dhawal Khaimar (Patil) vs. State of Maharashtra, State of Maharashtra vs. Sandeep @ Babloo Prakash Khairnar (Patil), Ram Anup Singh and Ors. vs. State of Bihar, Nazir Khan and Ors. vs. State of Delhi, Swamy Shraddananda (2) @ Murali Manohar Mishra vs. State of Kamataka, Haru Ghosh vs. State of West Bengal, Ramraj @ Nanhoo @ Bihnu vs. State of Chhattisgarh, Neel Kumar @ Anil Kumar vs. The State of Haryana, Sandeep vs. State of UP, Gurvail Singh @ Gala and Anr. vs. State of Punjab, Jagmohan Singh vs. State of U.P., Bachan Singh vs. State of Punjab
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed as the High Court's decision to commute the death sentence to life imprisonment with restrictions on remission was upheld, considering the gravity of the crime and the well-reasoned judgments of the Supreme Court over a decade.
other_sentence_order: The High Court directed that the accused should not be granted any remission until he served at least 20 years of imprisonment.
